data.narrative: Student demonstrated rigorous scientific methodology and intellectual honesty throughout Module 03 (Reproduction Science). In Step 2, the student selected synthetic reproduction (Option B) to isolate concurrent load on a single key while eliminating PII and compliance risks. In Step 3, the student built a minimal, portable asynchronous reproduction harness (scripts/repro_race.py). In Step 5 (BREAK), empirical stress testing at concurrency 25 with Redis offline revealed a critical architectural failure: SQLAlchemy QueuePool connection exhaustion (15 connections saturated, 10 timeouts at 30s). In Step 6 (FIX), the student decoupled database session checkout from external network I/O in redirect.py, bounding DB connections strictly to query execution (<1ms). Post-fix verification confirmed 100% redirect success at both concurrency 10 (10/10) and concurrency 25 (25/25), completely resolving QueuePool exhaustion. The student maintained rigorous integrity by transparently documenting that the original intermittent HTTP 500 remains unreproduced, noting persistent Redis-offline latency, and flagging a timing discrepancy in Test V2 as an unverified hypothesis.

dimension_scores.observation: Designed and implemented a surgical, minimal fix that bounded database connection lifetime to query execution (<1ms), returned connections immediately to QueuePool, and preserved all public API contracts (307, 404, 410) and tenant isolation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Extracted scalar link_info in DualRedirectResponse.__init__, closed session in finally block, and passed link_info to _resolve_async, achieving 25/25 HTTP 307 successes in stress verification.

dimension_scores.observation: Maintained strict technical integrity by refusing to fabricate test passes or claim the original HTTP 500 was resolved, clearly documenting that the 500 remains unconfirmed and identifying timing metrics as unverified hypotheses.
dimension_scores.evidence: Explicitly documented that HTTP 500 was not reproduced under offline Redis; flagged the ~117.3s latency vs ~111.1s batch duration timing discrepancy as an unverified hypothesis.
